 Storm Boelo latest: Flights cancelled as ‘danger to life’ weather warnings issued for 80mph winds
 Ferry and train services have also been halted as Storm Boelo hurtles towards UK bringing heavy rain and gales
 Maryam Zakir-Hussain Saturday 24 October 2026 19:30 BST

 Flights have been grounded after the Met Office issued fresh “danger to life” weather warnings for Storm Boelo.
 Dublin Airport announced several cancellations and delays on Saturday as the second named storm of the season hurtled towards the country bringing heavy rains and gales. 
 A post on social media said: “As of 12 noon, 5 outbound and 4 inbound flights have been cancelled by airlines due to weather issues.”
 Ferry services have also been halted between Ireland and Pembrokeshire, and more than a dozen rail services have been cancelled on Scotland’s west coast. 
 The travel chaos comes immediately after Storm Austen unleashed havoc on Friday, leaving thousands of home without power in Cornwall and causing schools to close. 
 On Saturday, the Met Office issued amber warnings for Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England as widespread gusts up to 70mph are forecast, rising to 80mph in coastal locations.
 A second amber warning covers parts of Northern Ireland, and a fresh yellow rain warning for Wales and parts of England was also issued.
 Key Points
 More than a dozen flights grounded as Storm Boelo wreaks havoc 
 What weather warnings are in place this weekend? 
 Rail disruption as 80mph gales hit UK 
 Ferry services halted due to severe weather conditions 
 Flood warnings in place in England 
 What should you buy for an emergency kit?
 An emergency kit filled with essentials for staying warm, food and water, as well as medical supplies, can help during power cuts and if it is unsafe to go outside.
 According to the Red Cross a home emergency unit should include:
 list of emergency contact numbers (paper copy, in case your phone loses power) 
 portable power bank 
 cash for essentials (like food or fuel) 
 torch and radio (battery or wind-up), spare batteries 
 essential medication (and backup power for medical equipment, if needed) 
 first aid kit (e.g., plasters, bandages, antiseptic, gloves) 
 hand sanitiser and wet wipes 
 three days’ supply of bottled water and long-life, ready-to-eat food (include a tin opener) 
 copies of important documents (kept in a waterproof bag) 
 pencil and paper 
 spare house and car keys 
 baby and pet supplies (if needed) 
 Blankets, spare clothes, hygiene products and a camping stove could also be useful in the event of power outages, the charity added.
 The Met Office also urges people to check forecasts and warnings regularly, ensuring homes and vehicles are ready for severe weather, and looking out for vulnerable friends, family members and neighbours can all help to reduce disruption when bad weather strikes.

 How to keep your home warm without huge energy bills, according to experts
 The UK is being hit by the second named storm of the season, as Storm Boelo , preceded by Austen, lashes the country.
 Parts of the UK and Ireland have been spending a lot of time in the single digits in recent days, serving as a stark reminder that winter is on the way.
 Staying comfortable during the colder months is important. The challenge, however, remains achieving this warmth without incurring excessive energy costs .
 How to keep your home warm without huge energy bills, according to experts 
 Keeping your home warm is important, but keeping bills low is vital too
 Maryam Zakir-Hussain 24 October 2026 18:00 
 Safari Park in Merseyside closed tomorrow
 Knowsley Safari Park in Prescot, Merseyside will be closed tomorrow due to the ongoing storm. 
 An update on the park’s Instagram page said: "Knowsley Safari will be closed tomorrow, Sunday October 25, to ensure the safety of our guests, animals and colleagues during the storm.
 "If you’re booked to visit us tomorrow, you will have received an email with details on how to rearrange your visit. If you didn’t receive this, please email safari.park@knowsley.com with your booking reference number and preferred date for your visit."
 Maryam Zakir-Hussain 24 October 2026 17:30 
 Dozens of flood warnings and alerts in Scotland 
 There are 16 flood warnings in Scotland, as of Saturday afternoon. 
 The warning mean “immediate action is required”. 
 They affect:
 Ayr to Troon 
 Largs 
 Upper Solway Firth 
 Southerness Point 
 Rough Firth 
 Outer Wigtown Bay 
 East Luce Bay 
 West Luce Bay North 
 South West Rhins 
 Loch Ryan 
 Whitesands 
 West Luce Bay South 
 Carse of Lennoch to Lochlane 
 Dumbarton 
 Vatersay Causeway 
 Berneray Causeway 
 There are also 11 flood alerts, which affect: 
 Aberdeenshire and Aberdeen City 
 Argyll and Bute 
 Ayrshire and Arran 
 Caithness and Sutherland 
 Dumfries and Galloway 
 Easter Ross and Great Glen 
 Findhorn, Nairn, Moray and Speyside 
 Orkney 
 Tayside 
 West Central Scotland 
 Western Isles 
 Maryam Zakir-Hussain 24 October 2026 17:00 
 Storm Boelo: Planes battle strong winds as they attempt to land at Heathrow
 Planes were filmed making a bumpy landing at Heathrow Airport as Storm Boelo brought strong winds and heavy rain to parts of the UK. (24 October)
 Flights have been grounded after the Met Office issued a “danger to life” weather warning as the storm swept across the country.
 Dublin Airport announced several cancellations on Saturday as the second named storm of the last few days brought heavy rain and powerful gusts.
 The disruption comes just a day after Storm Austen battered parts of the UK, leaving thousands of homes without power in Cornwall and forcing schools to close.
 Storm Boelo: Planes battle strong winds as they attempt to land at Heathrow 
 Maryam Zakir-Hussain 24 October 2026 16:51 
 Flood warnings in England
 There are now six flood warnings, where flooding is expected, in England. They affect:
 Cumbrian coastline from Gretna to Silloth including Port Carlisle, Skinburness and Rockcliffe 
 Cumbrian coastline from Silloth to St Bees, between Allonby and Whitehaven 
 Cumbrian coastline from Silloth to St Bees including Maryport, Flimby, Workington and Whitehaven 
 Cumbrian coastline from St Bees Head to Haverigg, along the coast from North Head to Haverigg 
 Irish Sea at New Brighton in Merseyside 
 Lee's Bridge at Astley Bridge Central, Bolton, Greater Manchester 
 More widely, there are 40 flood alerts, where flooding is possible, across the northern and southern coastal areas on the west of the country. 
 ( Environment Agency )

 Maryam Zakir-Hussain 24 October 2026 16:30 
 More than a dozen flights grounded as Storm Boelo wreaks havoc
 Over a dozen flights have been grounded as Storm Boelo wreaks havoc in the sky. 
 Dublin Airport gave a late afternoon update, announcing that 19 flights have been cancelled on Saturday, warning further disruption is expected. 
 The update on social media said: “As of 4pm, 9 outbound and 10 inbound flights have been cancelled by airlines due to weather issues. Six inbound flights performed go-arounds - 5 of which landed on the second attempt, with the other diverting to another airport before returning a short time later. Winds are forecast to remain strong for the rest of the day, which may lead to further disruption.”
